entries.why: My battery is running low and grit in my elbow joint is crunching.

entries.text: Sand got into his left elbow joint. Again.
Sold Mabel (a little landing strut) for 4 credits. Now has 9.
trading Mabel the landing strut for sweet, sweet credits
entries.why: i need some extra credits so I can grab that smooth tether grease later

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "Trading Mabel"

haggling over a dented fuel cell at the junk market
entries.why: I need more credits if I'm gonna buy slick grease for the tether spooler.

entries.text: Bought a little landing strut for 4 credits and named it Mabel. Has 2 left.
poking through trader piles for shiny wire and smooth lube
entries.why: My tether spooler needs smooth wire so it doesn't jam up! *bweep*

entries.text: Got paid 3 credits for the repair. Now has 6.
tinkering with a trader's jammed coupling unit
entries.why: Taking on a quick repair job at the market earns credits for fresh parts.

entries.text: The depot's cargo-hauler bot dropped a part and didn't notice.
Dug up a perfectly good bolt and named it Fen; a dented fuel cell and named it Tilly.
digging through scrap piles for shiny ship parts
entries.why: My stash is totally empty and the Little Dart needs good metal to grow.

entries.text: plugging into the charging dock for a quick boost
entries.why: My battery is running a bit low after wiring up that slip ring.

entries.text: The power flickered across the outpost for a few seconds.
Worked on the Little Dart Mk 28 (version 1, 8% built): wiring the 8-wire slip ring into the compact motorized tether spooler assembly (used Captain, half a thruster nozzle)
soldering eight tiny tether leads to the new rotary slip ring
entries.why: The tether spooler needs clean continuous power while spinning full tilt.
entries.detail: wiring the 8-wire slip ring into the compact motorized tether spooler assembly

entries.text: Idea: Design a rotating mount for the Little Dart's main listening dish using an eight-wire slip ring so it spins endlessly.
Read "Fathom Spool Assembly": An eight-wire slip ring lets a spool spin completely around without tangling up any electrical tethers.
esmats.eu wouldn't open, so he tried bluerobotics.com instead.
reading about electrodynamic tether lubrication at the comms tower
entries.why: i need to see how to stop the tether spooler from friction-heating when it rolls out.

entries.text: perched on the dune ridge, pointing my brass dish at the starry sky
entries.why: I haven't spent time stargazing in way too long and my curiosity is twitching.

entries.text: zooming to the fuel depot for a fresh cup of oil
entries.why: my gears are feeling a bit dry and sluggish after all that tinkering.

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "Oil stop!"
